notes.title: GDS - Dec Patch Notes & Dev Update
notes.content:
Hey there, Game Directors! We’ve been hard at work on the full game, but we wanted to get one last demo update before we say goodbye to 2021.

[h3]Preview Character Impact:[/h3]
Previously, when the player made a choice in conversation, there was no option to tell whether this would impact a character negatively or positively. In this update we’ve added this as an option for players who want to see how a character will react before making a choice.
[list]
[*] Added ability to preview which characters will be impacted by a choice (based on the difficulty setting in Options)
[*] Minor UI adjustments for all aspect ratios
[*] Preview and Impact (after a decision) values were updated to use the same system 
[/list]

[h3]Bug Fixes & other improvements:[/h3]
[list]
[*] Adjusted a Tala conversation impact and character emote to better reflect the intent
[*] Fixed some of the ‘game fail’ ending screens
[*] Some minor text updates & typos
[/list]

Thanks again for playing our demo. Send us your feedback via the survey, or reach out to us on [url=https://twitter.com/DoubleBlit]Twitter[/url] or the forums here on Steam. We’d love to hear from you!

We wish you all a fantastic holiday season!

- The GDS team

notes.title: GDS - Aug Patch Notes & Dev Update
notes.content:
Hey there, Game Directors! We’ve made some big changes to the demo since our last update, and are excited for you to try them out.


You’ll now notice a functional options screen with difficulty settings, and a new tooltip system to provide a greater depth of information on status bars and icons. We’ve also introduced Victor, an entirely new character and another face of the publisher that was concepted live during our LudoNarraCon stream. We hope you enjoy the new changes, and as always, let us know what you think!


Onward with the details of this update:

[h3]Options screen:[/h3]
[list]
[*] Functional options screen allowing you to change video, audio and game difficulty settings
[*] Game difficulty settings includes 3 difficulty presets (Easy, Default, Hard)
[*] Game difficulty settings allows for customizing individual elements in presets - including whether to show (or hide) stakeholder preview & impact, character impact, and conversation patience
[*] Show/Hide difficulty settings includes whether this is reflected in the animation (such as stakeholder icon animation showing if the choice will impact this stakeholder positively or negatively), as well as the tooltip data (where relevant, such as showing or hiding the numerical impact to a stakeholder)
[/list]

[h3]Tooltips:[/h3]
[list]
[*] Most game icons and Options screen difficulty settings now have tooltips providing more information on what they do
[*] Where relevant, game icons also include numerical values (such as the value of a stakeholder bar, or the impact a conversation choice will have), unless this was turned off in the Options settings
[/list]

[h3]New character art:[/h3]
[list]
[*] Victor, the character concepted on a live stream has been added to the game, including his emotes.
  [i][b]Thanks to everyone that participated in that stream & created this character. If you'd like to see more events like that let us know.[/b][/i]
[/list]

[h3]Bug Fixes & other improvements:[/h3]
[list]
[*] Victor's conversation has been updated to suit his personality better & take advantage of his emotes 
[*] Fixed an issue where a conversation with Phil could sneak into day 15 and not end up selectable
[*] Fixed an issue where hitting game over as the day was ending would only trigger the game over at start of new day, after the checkpoint save, which meant players could not continue from the start of the day as usual (they'd hit the game over at start of day), and needed to restart completely 
[*] With tooltips being a thing, we've removed the stakeholder icon titles text from the UI
[*] Clock advancing rapidly (such as when passing time) now has a subtle clock tick sound to draw attention to it
[*] Fixed a few issues that crept up as part of adding Options/Tooltips, but were promptly squashed
[/list]

[h3]Survey:[/h3]
[list]
[*] The survey link has been updated, allowing players that previously sent feedback to send more feedback again.
[/list]

Thanks again for playing our demo. Send us your feedback via the survey, or reach out to us on [url=https://twitter.com/DoubleBlit]Twitter [/url]or the Forums here on Steam. We’d love to hear from you!

- The GDS team

notes.title: GDS - June Patch Notes & Dev Update
notes.content:
Happy pride month everyone!

As the team continues working on the full game, it's time to bring some of those improvements & bug 
fixes over to the demo.  We were hoping to have this update out earlier this month, but have been wrestling with a few tricky bugs. 

In our last update we talked about moving from a static sequence of conversations to our new Systemic Story System.  This system is intended to introduce more variability in the types of conversations that the player encounters in each playthrough.  It has been huge for us in terms of unlocking narrative flexibility for the full game.

In addition, GDS was part of [url=https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=Ozqhc7YXd3M]Wholesome Games Direct[/url] this month, as well as in the Wholesome section of the Guerrilla Collective event here on Steam!  We hope you had a chance to check out some of the other amazing games. As a reminder, be sure to give them all a Follow & Wishlist - it's a huge help for upcoming games, and a great way to support those devs.

Onward with the changes in this update:

[h3]Updates to chat:[/h3]
[list]
[*] Characters now include their pronouns
[*] Fixed an elusive bug with the player choice buttons (see bug fixes below for more info)
[/list]

[h3]Updates to intro/tutorial:[/h3]
[list]
[*] More recent images
[*] Reflects the character impact change from previous update
[*] Based on feedback, removes the fake vertical scrollbar that was confusing some players
[/list]

[h3]Bug Fixes:[/h3]
[list]
[*] Fixed some issues related to the system story system
[*] Fixed a bug where quickly clicking on a choice would make that button not show text on subsequent choices
[*] Fixed a logic issue on Tala's conversation on day 14, where some choices would repeat
[*] Fixed a few typos and minor text tweaks
[/list]

Thanks again for playing our demo.  Please send us your feedback, either through the survey link you can find in the game menus, or reach out to us on [url=https://twitter.com/DoubleBlit]Twitter [/url]or the Forums here on Steam. 

- The GDS team

notes.title: GDS - April Patch Notes & Dev Update
notes.content:
It has been a while since our last update, and we know we’ve been a bit quiet - we really appreciate your patience!

The team has been hard at work on the full game. In fact, much of the work in the last few months has been behind the scenes in service of that.

However, in time for LudoNarraCon, we made a small update to the demo. Below are some more details on what we’ve been up to, as well as what is included in the demo update.

[h3]Character Impact Notifications:[/h3]
[list]
[*] Based on feedback, there is now a notification area that shows when decisions impact specific characters either positively or negatively, as well as indicate if that was a small, medium or large impact.
[*] Previously the only impacts seen were the status icons, so it was not always easy to understand how characters ended up reaching their frayed states.
[*] A future update will include the ability to control how much of this information you want showing on the UI, as part of a difficulty & accessibility setting.
[/list]

[h3]Additional Conversations & New Location:[/h3]
[list]
[*] Some changes were made to the ending scenes.
[*] Some more conversations that occur in the demo time frame were added.
[*] A new location has been added to the demo.
[/list]

[h3]Bug Fixes:[/h3]
[list]
[*] Tracked down a rare bug where the player could get stuck because no conversation options were presented.
[*] Several text edits & typo fixes.
[/list]

[h3]Changes We’re Working On:[/h3]

[b]Systemic Story System:[/b]
One of the big changes we've been able to make, which does exist in the demo but is not noticeable, is that we've successfully moved the story away from being hard coded on specific days to now playing out relative to your progress with conversations. Conversations are no longer restricted  to occur on specific days, and instead trigger after certain prerequisites have been satisfied. This means the game can also now add new days or skip days as needed, depending on the number of conversations available.

That's a pretty fundamental change that unlocks the flexibility we wanted for building out the rest of the game story, and the unique mix of story layers based on what occurs in each game phase and each game event in a phase, and have those play nicely with the on-going character arcs and general random events which can largely occur at any time (as long as certain prerequisites are met).  

That's a bit hard to show in the demo as it is only focused on a single event inside of a game phase, and purposefully structured in a more controlled way so you always get essentially the same experience in that timeframe - but as we add more content it'll really pay off, and we're excited to get some of that into a future demo update for you to see for yourselves!

Thanks again for playing our demo.  Please send us your feedback, and we’d love to see you at one of our upcoming streams as part of LudoNarraCon!  You can see the schedule below.

     - The GDS team

notes.title: Demo Update 3
notes.content:
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/37888392/6e58baa132800b1fb4f79b83c2af424b088dca9c.jpg[/img]

[h3]Updated Game Director Story Demo[/h3]
The year is almost done - and it's been quite the year for most of us.  We're looking forward to a holiday break and hope all of you, your friends, and family are safe & that you have a fantastic holiday season and a better new year.

In our last post we talked about our date move to 2021, and we're excited to share more about that soon.  In the meantime, while we're working on the full game, we will continue to make some updates to the demo to get early feedback from you, address any issues you told us about, as well as to keep it as close of a representation of what you can expect in the final game as possible.

In this update we’re adding some bug fixes to items you reported, but most notably we're adding a much asked save/load system, a new game presentation featuring larger characters and a cleaner chat UI, a festive theme, and more!  We'd love to hear what you think, particularly on the new UI.

Here is the full list of changes made in this update, which are now available in the demo on Steam.

[h3]Save/Load[/h3]
[list]
[*] The game now autosaves at the end of each day. 
[*] From the main menu, if you have a save game, the option to 'Continue' will appear.
[*] From the main menu, if you have a save game, pressing 'New Game' will warn you that it will overwrite the previous save. (The full game will have multiple save slots, but for the demo only the one save slot exists)
[/list]

[h3]Updated main game UI[/h3]
[list]
[*] The newer UI is now in the demo.
[*] The new UI places the stakeholder impact icons at the bottom, closer to the the choice buttons, making it easier to preview impacts as you roll over decisions.
[*] The new UI has a larger character image for whoever is speaking, allowing you to see their emotes/frayed states better.
[*] The new UI has a cleaner look and partial transparency, allowing you to see more of the background art.
[/list]

[h3]Additional conversations & a new location added[/h3]
[list]
[*] Some additional conversations that occur in the demo timeframe were added.  
[*] A cozy Cafe location has been added. For the moment, one of the demo conversations takes place here. No spoilers though, you'll have to play it to see these. 
[/list]

[h3]Other Quality of Life improvements[/h3]
[list]
[*] Just in time for the holidays, the team has decorated the office. The options buttons were moved to accommodate some of the decorations.
[*] The epilogue screens when successfully completing the demo now include images for each of the characters it references.
[*] Additional balancing of some of the hidden tracked values, like 'work-life balance'.
[*] Spread out the timing of when some conversations appeared (reducing the chance you'll miss these).
[/list]

[h3]Bug fixes[/h3]
[list]
[*] Game correctly supports 16x10 aspect ratio on all screens.
[*] Several fixes and tweaks to the ending scene for the E3 event to reflect characters being in/out of office correctly.
[*] Several text edits & typo fixes throughout the demo days story beats.
[*] Fixed a Tala conversation that had a Khepri icon.
[*] Fixed an issue where players could inadvertently select a menu item before the menu came up.
[/list]

Have any feedback on this update or for future ones? We'd love to hear it. Fill out the survey on the menus, or feel free to shoot us a message here on the Steam community, or through our Twitter account (@doubleblit)

Thanks for playing the demo,
The Game Director Story team

notes.title: Release date change
notes.content:
Hi everyone,

If you’re reading this there’s a good chance you took the time to play or wishlist Game Director Story, and for that we’re grateful.

Today, we made the decision to postpone our launch to 2021. Initially, we targeted late 2020 as our window, but the realities of indie development have made it clear that it’s best for us to push it into the new year.

The Game Director Story team is a small group of talented developers who balance other jobs, families, and school. We’re extremely thankful for their time and want to be able to continue to honor that balance in their lives, while building Game Director Story into the best game we know it can be. 

One of the main motivations behind making Game Director Story is to take a hard look at some of the industry’s biggest problems. Because of this, we feel it's important for us to play our part in setting a better example of how things can be done. We know it’s the right thing to give our team the space and flexibility they need.

We are extremely motivated and look forward to making more progress on the game. We don’t know exactly when in 2021 the game will be ready, but we’ll have a better picture in the new year, which we will share with you.

In the meantime, we updated the demo [url=https://store.steampowered.com/app/1305180/Game_Director_Story/]last week[/url], and we’d love to hear what you think. Feel free to drop us a line on our [url=https://twitter.com/DoubleBlit]Twitter [/url] or here on the Steam community any time!

Thanks for your understanding,
Fernando & the GDS team

notes.title: Demo Update 2
notes.content:
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/37888392/6e58baa132800b1fb4f79b83c2af424b088dca9c.jpg[/img]

[h3]Updated Game Director Story Demo[/h3]
Earlier this summer, we launched an early demo of Game Director Story in time for the Steam Summer Festival. We wanted to give folks a small sample of our game for a limited time, but ended up getting so much great feedback from the community that we decided to leave the demo up.

Since then, we continue working on the game, and have made a few updates to the demo to address feedback from players, like making it clearer when new conversations are coming in or leaving the chat window, and how the game’s clock advances.

We’ve also added some key functionality that better represents the intended final game that we weren't able to get in time for the summer demo, such as not being able to freely switch between different conversations.

Today we’re rolling out an updated demo with these improvements and a number of bug fixes. We’re grateful for your input, and look forward to introducing more features (like a coming UI refresh) as we keep making progress on the game.

Here are all the changes we’ve made in this update, which are now available in the demo here on our steam page.


[h3]Improvements to Conversation Flow[/h3]
[list]
[*] Players can now swap between available conversations prior to starting a chat, as well as at any point where a chat choice can be made. 
[*] Conversation icons are now greyed out mid-chat to indicate if you cannot swap at that moment and must wait for the next chat choice.
[*] When a chat is complete you no longer need to close it, you can now select another conversation from the list.
[*] If the list of conversations is full and there are conversations that have been completed but not closed, the next new conversations will automatically replace/close the oldest completed conversation.
[*] Conversation icons now animate in/out of the chat window, so it is more obvious when conversations expire, or are replaced with a new conversation.
[/list]

[h3]Improvements to Game Clock[/h3]
[list]
[*] The time of day clock now advances per conversation line.
[*] If all available conversations are done, the time of day clock will fast forward to the next available conversation that day (or to the end of day prompt).
[/list]

[h3]Tutorial Updates[/h3]
[list]
[*] The tutorial screen was updated to better fit the overall art style.
[*] You can now skip the tutorial if you’ve already seen it.
[*] The tutorial is now available in the main game scene by clicking the “?” icon.
[/list]

[h3]Quality of Life improvements[/h3]
[list]
[*] When your game ends before reaching the end of the 15th day in the demo, the result screens now indicate what day you made it to.
[*] We added a second music track during gameplay, so you don't have to keep listening to the same track on repeat.
[/list]

[h3]Bug fixes[/h3]
[list]
[*] The pause menu and tutorial screens (in game) now correctly pause the chat.
[*] The end of the demo now always reflects Khepri’s story result correctly.
[*] You can now click to skip the text quote at the start of the game.
[*] Some more space was added at the top of the chat, so characters with big ears were not as cut off (we’re lookin at you Phil!).
[*] The chat window sun icon now reflects the time of day correctly.
[*] Updated the out-of-game survey & removed other in-game mentions of the Steam Summer Festival, now that we're keeping the demo up.
[*] Several text edits throughout the demo days story beats.
[/list]

Have any feedback on this update or for future ones? We'd love to hear it. Fill out the survey on the menus, or feel free to shoot us a message here on the Steam community, or through our Twitter account (@doubleblit)

Thanks for playing the demo,
The Game Director Story team

notes.title: Demo updates now live
notes.content:
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/37888392/6e58baa132800b1fb4f79b83c2af424b088dca9c.jpg[/img]

[h3]Early game over feedback[/h3]
If the game ends before the number of days is finished, you now also get some information on why it failed.  Reaching the end of demo (day 0) also has multiple endings depending on your decisions.

[h3]Link to the web survey[/h3]
In the end screens we've also added a link to optional open a web browser and go to the demo feedback survey - we greatly appreciate your feedback from this early demo.

[h3]Text too fast[/h3]
One comment that kept coming up was text being too fast to keep up.  In the final game this will be part of the game options, but for the demo there's a few things you can now do to manage text speed:
[list]
[*] Text was made a little slower again by default
[*] You can click left mouse button or press space bar to advance text
[*] You can now scroll up to continue reading text, and new lines added do not bump you to bottom of chat window
[/list]

[h3]Editing pass of text[/h3]
There was another editing pass across the whole demo to make text clearer, as well as some spelling errors

[h3]Next/Previous buttons in intro & outro (end game) screens more visible[/h3]
Some players found it hard to spot the arrows with the previous color scheme.  The arrow button colors were changed to stand out more easily.

Have other feedback or issues in the demo? Send us some feedback!

Thanks for playing the demo,
The Game Director Story team

notes.title: About Game Director Story
notes.content:
First off, thank you for participating in the Steam Game Festival and supporting indie games!

[h3][b]About Game Director Story[/b][/h3]
In Game Director Story our goal is to take you behind-the-scenes and provide you a sense of what it is like to try and develop a AAA (large blockbuster) game, while still keeping the experience of playing GDS entertaining and accessible for anyone.

[h3][b]About the Demo[/b][/h3]
The demo we have in the Steam Game Festival is a portion of an Event from the full game, and can take ~30-45m to play through, not including variations from replay.  

In the full game you will experience all major phases of development, from concept to post ship, and within each phase you may encounter several iconic Events - situations that challenge you and your team, usually with a very short deadline.  

For the Steam Game Festival demo, the Event is based on a last minute request from your publisher to have a part of your game ready in time to present at E3, a notable industry tradeshow, but well ahead of your current schedule.

[h3][b]Why are we doing this?[/b][/h3]
You do not have to search too hard to find articles about difficult game productions, industry
challenges, or toxic fandom. But few players (unless they are devs themselves) have ever been on a team trying to cope from being directly impacted by these issues, and even most devs have not had the opportunity to be in the room when those kinds of decisions are made, let alone in a position to influence or outright make the decision.

In addition, while there is a growing interest by players and fans in the overall process of making games, and support for developers as more of them bring their stories to light, the industry in general remains quite insular, secretive and closed off to most outsiders.

Unlike most games about gamedev, Game Director Story is based on first-hand accounts - with creative license used in order to adapt these to the game mechanics, and of course to change names etc - and made by a team that collectively has multiple decades of experience in AAA game dev and publishing, in addition to contributions from other industry veterans.

To be clear, Game Director Story is not an expose of any specific individuals, companies or situations. However, as a dev you will likely recognize many of the situations in GDS as sadly these issues tend to be fairly common across most dev teams & game cycles. 

Game Director Story is also not about the macro management of making something - for example, you don't hire more 'skillset widgets' to make a progress bar go faster.  GDS focuses on the various relationships that you must forge, and maintain, as a Game Director in order to have the influence needed to accomplish your goal.

As a player, by placing you in the role of having to make those decisions, and seeing the impact of these play out on your team members, we hope to provide you a unique perspective - as well as a better understanding - of the process of making games, and the toll it can take on those that make them.

Please visit us on the Steam forum and let us know what you think - there is a link to a survey that we'd greatly appreciate you filling out once you've played the demo.

Thanks again from all of us at Double Blit.
